headline: Over 2,300 tourists stranded as Army exchanges fire with armed group in Sajek
summary: A road blockade by local organizations led to a massive tourist jam and a shootout between security forces and the UPDF near Ujo Bazar.
details: Approximately 2,300 tourists were stranded on their way back from Sajek Valley after two local organizations launched an indefinite road blockade on Thursday morning.
The protest, led by the Sajek Karbari Association and Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee, demanded the removal of armed members of the JSS (Santu Larma) from the area.
Violence erupted near Ujo Bazar when law enforcers attempted to clear the blockade. Protesters reportedly threw stones and brickbats, leading to some tourists being injured.
According to police and ISPR, the Bangladesh Army exchanged fire with an armed group, identified by police as the UPDF, to bring the situation under control.
The UPDF has denied the shootout, claiming the reports are fabricated and alleging that security forces opened fire on peaceful protesters.
Following baton charges by law enforcers, the blockade was dispersed, and the tourist convoy was safely escorted to Khagrachari around 11:00 am.
The district administration had temporarily closed the Sajek Valley Tourist Centre for safety, ordering all tourists to leave the valley by 4:00 pm on Thursday.
caption:
2,300 tourists trapped in a blockade, stones thrown, and a shootout between the Army and an armed group in Sajek.

Approximately 2,300 tourists were stranded on their way back from Sajek Valley after two local organizations launched an indefinite road blockade on Thursday morning.

The protest, led by the Sajek Karbari Association and Sajek Gono Odhikar Rokkha Committee, demanded the removal of armed members of the JSS (Santu Larma) from the area.

Violence erupted near Ujo Bazar when law enforcers attempted to clear the blockade. Protesters reportedly threw stones and brickbats, leading to some tourists being injured.

According to police and ISPR, the Bangladesh Army exchanged fire with an armed group, identified by police as the UPDF, to bring the situation under control.

The UPDF has denied the shootout, claiming the reports are fabricated and alleging that security forces opened fire on peaceful protesters.

Following baton charges by law enforcers, the blockade was dispersed, and the tourist convoy was safely escorted to Khagrachari around 11:00 am.

The district administration had temporarily closed the Sajek Valley Tourist Centre for safety, ordering all tourists to leave the valley by 4:00 pm on Thursday.

headline_marked: Man [[beaten to death]] at Suhrawardy Hospital on child abductor suspicion
headline: Man beaten to death at Suhrawardy Hospital on child abductor suspicion
summary: A 41-year-old man, claimed by his family to be mentally unstable, was killed by a mob at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital.
details: A 41-year-old man named Alam Sheikh was beaten to death by a mob at Dhaka's Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital late Wednesday night.
The incident occurred around 11pm when Sheikh was roaming in front of the children's ward, causing suspicion among the families of children receiving treatment.
When questioned, Sheikh was reportedly unable to provide a satisfactory answer, leading a group of people to drag him downstairs and beat him severely until he died on the spot.
The family of the deceased, a resident of Rupnagar, Dhaka, claims that Alam Sheikh was mentally unstable.
Tejgaon Division Police Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan stated that the police recovered the body after receiving a report via the national emergency service number 999.
Police have detained one person, identified as the mastermind of the incident, and confirmed that a case will be filed against him.
The body has been sent to the Shaheed Suhrawardy Hospital morgue for a postmortem examination.
caption:
A man suspected of being a child abductor was beaten to death by a mob at a Dhaka hospital.

A 41-year-old man named Alam Sheikh was beaten to death by a mob at Dhaka's Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital late Wednesday night.

The incident occurred around 11pm when Sheikh was roaming in front of the children's ward, causing suspicion among the families of children receiving treatment.

When questioned, Sheikh was reportedly unable to provide a satisfactory answer, leading a group of people to drag him downstairs and beat him severely until he died on the spot.

The family of the deceased, a resident of Rupnagar, Dhaka, claims that Alam Sheikh was mentally unstable.

Tejgaon Division Police Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan stated that the police recovered the body after receiving a report via the national emergency service number 999.

Police have detained one person, identified as the mastermind of the incident, and confirmed that a case will be filed against him.

The body has been sent to the Shaheed Suhrawardy Hospital morgue for a postmortem examination.
